plan: In a single-round auction with independent value draws, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. With a private value of $23, I want to win if possible, but avoid overpaying. Given the $0-$49 uniform distribution, other bidders' values are likely around $25. I'll bid $22 - this gives me a chance to win while protecting my potential profit margin. If my bid is second-highest, I lose nothing. If I win at $22, I'll profit if my value exceeds the second-highest bid.

In a first-price sealed bid auction with independent private values, the optimal strategy is complex. My value is $18. I want to bid strategically to maximize expected profit. Since this is a one-round game with no history, I'll aim to bid slightly below my true value, anticipating other bidders might also bid strategically. A bid around $15-16 seems reasonable - low enough to potentially win while preserving profit margin if I win.

With a private value of $39, I want to bid strategically. Since values are randomly drawn, other bidders might have lower or higher values. A good strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. I'll aim to bid around $35-$37 - high enough to likely win, but low enough to minimize overpaying. This creates a buffer that protects my potential earnings if I win while avoiding overbidding.
